articles.title: Irlanda corta su rueda de prensa tras una acusación de racismo
articles.standfirst: La comparecencia de Heimir Hallgrimsson fue trasladada a otra sala tras la acusación, sin la presencia de los medios israelíes
articles.summary: La comparecencia de Heimir Hallgrimsson fue trasladada a otra sala tras la acusación, sin la presencia de los medios israelíes
articles.body: La tensión entre Irlanda e Israel ha vuelto a trasladarse fuera de los terrenos de juego. La rueda de prensa previa al encuentro de la Nations League entre ambas selecciones terminó abruptamente después de que un periodista israelí acusara de racismo a los jugadores irlandeses. El oficial de prensa de la Federación Irlandesa de Fútbol (FAI), Kieran Crowley, rechazó tajantemente las acusaciones y las calificó de "completamente falsas". El incidente se produjo en un ambiente especialmente delicado, después de que ambos combinados ya protagonizaran varios episodios de tensión en su primer enfrentamiento, disputado el pasado 27 de septiembre en Debrecen (Hungría). Irlanda se impuso por 0-3, con los goles de Troy Parrott, Adam Idah y Jack Moylan, en un encuentro marcado también por los gestos de protesta de los futbolistas irlandeses durante el himno israelí y la ausencia de saludos protocolarios entre los capitanes. La polémica se trasladó posteriormente a las declaraciones del capitán israelí, Manor Solomon, quien aseguró que esperaba con ganas el siguiente partido y afirmó: "Obviamente, nos odian y nosotros no les tenemos cariño". También defendió a su país con unas palabras que generaron controversia: "Tenemos un país diez veces mejor que el suyo". La tensión ha vuelto a aumentar durante la comparecencia previa al segundo encuentro. Varios periodistas israelíes plantearon preguntas ajenas al ámbito deportivo y, posteriormente, uno de ellos acusó al delantero irlandés, Adam Idah, de haber llamado 'monos' a los jugadores israelíes durante el partido anterior. Kieran Crowley interrumpió la rueda de prensa y abandonó la sala junto al seleccionador, Heimir Hallgrímsson, para continuar atendiendo a los medios en otra estancia, sin la presencia de los periodistas israelíes. El conflicto entre ambas selecciones también está relacionado con las diferencias políticas derivadas de la guerra en Gaza. En Irlanda se han producido protestas y peticiones para que la selección no dispute estos encuentros, mientras que la Federación Irlandesa de Fútbol ha defendido su celebración. El segundo enfrentamiento, previsto para este domingo, se disputará en el TSC Arena de Bačka Topola, en Serbia, a puerta cerrada. De este modo, el partido correspondiente a la Nations League llega rodeado de una polémica que ha trascendido ampliamente el ámbito deportivo.

articles.title: IND vs BRA: From Chennai to Bhopal, Brazil supporters bring samba flair to Kolkata
articles.summary: TimesofIndia.com in Kolkata: People from different walks of life made their way to the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata for the historic India versus Brazil
articles.body: TimesofIndia.com in Kolkata: People from different walks of life made their way to the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata for the historic India versus Brazil friendly. Even though the iconic venue wasn't filled to its 65,000 capacity, many were still keen on making the most of this once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. A family of six from Chennai. A Brazilian living in Delhi. A family with two young boys from Delhi. Another family had travelled from Bhopal with their two daughters.Kohana had her husband and four boys for company. They went through India and Brazil jerseys on the street adjacent to the venue. The father went through them one by one while the four boys tested the size by placing the jerseys against themselves."We live in Chennai but we're from Japan. We bought tickets last week and have travelled just for this match. I'm supporting both teams today but the boys are big fans of the Brazilian team," said Kohana, who hails from Osaka, with a smile."We wanted to stay for the Uruguay game also but because they have school next week, we'll do just the Brazil match," she said, referring to the next FIFA friendly on October 6.Forty-six-year-old Felipe, who comes from Porto Alegre, the birthplace of Ronaldinho, has taken the trip from New Delhi. He works in the tourism sector in the capital with the aim of bringing more Brazilians, like himself, to travel to India.The moment he heard about the match, he didn't hesitate to buy a ticket online. Mere hours after arriving in Kolkata, he was overwhelmed by the city's food offerings."I never thought Brazil would come here. When I saw the Brazilian team was coming to India, I decided that no matter what, no matter how, I have to be there. I have to see this match," he said, revealing that he had spent around €150 on the ticket (Rs 16,000)."I like the city. I like the food, it is very good. I went to the Victoria Memorial, it's beautiful. I went to the New Market, a lot of things to see and buy," he continued.Adeeba and Aneefa Warsi donned the yellow and green of Brazil as they readied themselves outside the Salt Lake Stadium. Adeeba sported some bling to go with the outfit and had the colours of India and Brazil painted on both cheeks. The two sisters from Bhopal were joined by their parents for this big contest.For Aneefa, this wasn't just about watching India or Brazil play. It was also a chance for her, a footballer herself, to learn some things from the professionals."I hope to get inspired by the players and learn some new stuff. This is my first time watching a match, so I want to get better also," she said.Her elder sister chimed in by saying, "For me, this is an outing as well. I watch football also, so this is an experience for me also. So I want to see the scope of football in the country and take up the sport myself in the future," said the first-year college student.For the past month, since the tickets were bought, the duo spent sleepless nights. The preparations had begun well in advance. Even a night ago, as they arrived in the city, the match remained the topic of conversation."When to buy the jersey, where to buy it from? What kind of makeup to do? What look to show? What to wear? articles.title: Lamine el 'rápido' deja loco a De la Fuente con otro golazo
articles.standfirst: El extremo abrió la lata en el minuto seis de partido ante la República Checa.
articles.summary: El extremo abrió la lata en el minuto seis de partido ante la República Checa.
articles.body: jugar con Lamine Yamal en tu equipo es -casi- trampa. La versión que está mostrando durante este parón de selecciones es tan extraordinaria que se hace difícil encontrar adjetivos para describirlo. Además, a los trucos ya conocidos ha incorporado uno más: marcar rápido. Contra Inglaterra puso el 0-1 en el marcador antes de que su cumpliese el minuto dos de partido, contra Croacia vio puerta a los 104 segundos y frente a la República Checa cantamos su gol en el minuto seis de partido. Tremendo. Es la primera vez que marca en tres partidos consecutivos con la selección, pero la realidad es que no hay barreras para esta versión de Lamine. En los últimos 9 partidos acumula 12 goles y 7 asistencias. Cifras escandalosas que ha logrado engordar en este parón: gol ante Inglaterra, doblete y asistencia frente a Croacia y gol ante la República Checa. Sublime. En el Carlos Tartiere, Lamine sólo tardó unos segundos en encandilar al público. Gozó de su primera oportunidad en el minuto uno y levantó a la grada en el seis cuando cruzó un balón desde el vértice del área hasta la escuadra contraria de la portería defendida por Kinsky. Cuando lo extraordinario se repite habitualmente corre el riesgo de convertirse en banal, pero no por ello deja de ser extraordinario. El golazo de Lamine es el ejemplo perfecto y sólo hay que ver la reacción de Luis de la Fuente, que resopló llevándose las dos manos a la cabeza, par darse cuenta de la grandeza de lo que acababa de hacer. El gol ante la República Checa es el undécimo de Lamine Yamal con la camiseta de la selección española en los 36 partidos que ha disputado con sólo 19 años. Un registro sensacional para un campeón del mundo y de Europa. El hecho de que España llegase al descanso venciendo 2-0 hizo que Luis de la Fuente pudiese dejar a Lamine en el banquillo tras los primeros 45 minutos. "Para nosotros lo más importante es la salud de los futbolistas", viene repitiendo el técnico riojano. En el caso de Lamine, completó los 90 minutos en Wembley, 68 en Sevilla y sólo 45 en Oviedo.

articles.title: Minnesota upsets Michigan to beat Wolverines for the first time in 12 years
articles.summary: The Wolverines have lost back-to-back games and are now 3-2. Or 2-3 if you're a Western Michigan fan.
articles.body:
A week after losing to Iowa, Michigan lost again.

The Wolverines were upset 20-14 at Minnesota on Saturday after they turned the ball over on downs with 32 seconds to go in yet another ugly offensive performance.

It's Minnesota's first win over Michigan since 2014 and just the second in the last 40 years for the Gophers. It's also the first win for Minnesota at home over Michigan since 1977.

Michigan's offense gained just 180 yards on 49 plays as Bryce Underwood struggled. The sophomore was just 10-of-21 passing and threw interceptions on consecutive passes in the second half.

Minnesota cut the lead to 14-13 after the first interception, needing eight plays to go 34 yards. Underwood was then hit as he threw, and Zack Harden picked him off.

A play later, Minnesota was inside the 5-yard line thanks to a 31-yard run by Noah Jennings, and then QB Drake Lindsey found Darius Taylor for the go-ahead touchdown.

What are the answers for Michigan's offense?

The Wolverines' 52-17 win over UTEP in Week 3 looks more and more like an aberration.

Michigan has now failed to score more than 19 points in any of its other four games this season. It's a staggering stat given the promise that Underwood had shown as a freshman and the success that coach Kyle Whittingham and coordinator Jason Beck had with their offense at Utah in 2025.

Instead, Underwood has thrown one more touchdown (five) than he has interceptions (four) and isn't completing 60% of his passes.

The run game can't get unlocked, either. Jordan Marshall rushed 10 times for 50 yards and freshman Savion Hiter had eight carries for 9 yards.

After the game, Whittingham said this season has been the biggest challenge he's faced.

That's quite the statement. Whittingham was incredibly successful at Utah after taking over for Urban Meyer. But he was also hired into a Michigan athletic department that was in the midst of serious turmoil following the abrupt firing of Sherrone Moore and the upcoming transition from current athletic director Warde Manuel.

Things aren't getting any easier after Michigan's bye week in Week 6, either. The Wolverines play Penn State on Oct. 17 before hosting Indiana on Oct. 24. There's a very real chance that Michigan could start Big Ten play 0-4.

Minnesota, meanwhile, is now 4-1 and 2-0 in the Big Ten. The Gophers will be heavily favored at Purdue in Week 6, before three straight games against ranked opponents in No. 14 Iowa, No. 6 Indiana and No. 23 UCLA.

articles.title: No. 3 Notre Dame pulls away in second half at North Carolina as CJ Carr totals 5 TDs
articles.summary: Right after halftime, UNC made it a 1-point game, thanks to a 98-yard kickoff return, but the Fighting Irish didn't flinch.
articles.body:
North Carolina coupled a goal-line stand with a masterful 15-play, 97-yard touchdown drive to draw within a score of No. 3 Notre Dame before intermission on Saturday in a rainy Chapel Hill.

Then, in the first moments of the second half, UNC wide receiver Jaden Jefferson authored a 98-yard kick return touchdown to make it a one-point game.

That's as close as Bill Belichick's squad got to matching the Fighting Irish.

Marcus Freeman's steely Notre Dame won its 15th consecutive game dating back to last season by navigating that mid-game adversity brilliantly. The Irish responded with 16 unanswered points and wound up winning 37-26, behind five total CJ Carr touchdowns.

Carr, a 2027 NFL Draft prospect, carried the offensive load early for Notre Dame (5-0). He and wideout Jordan Faison were in lockstep. Throughout the day, they connected eight times for 132 yards and two touchdowns. Carr clocked out 21 of 29 with 234 yards through the air, 4 passing touchdowns and 1 rushing score.

Notre Dame's ground game came to life in the second half on the soggy Chris Smith Field at Kenan Stadium. The Irish picked up 166 of their 241 rushing yards in the second half. In doing so, they put away a game adversely affected by the conditions, so much so that each team's holder botched long snaps on extra points.

Freshman running back Jonaz Walton finished with 120 yards on 23 carries.

UNC (2-2, 0-1 ACC) dropped its second straight game after a 2-0 start. The Tar Heels let a 17-3 advantage slip against Clemson on Sept. 19 . The only lead UNC had this time was of the 7-0 variety, but its competitiveness is noteworthy following a mostly dismal 4-8 campaign a year ago.

Tar Heels quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. went 17 of 28 with 208 passing yards and three touchdowns, except he also tossed a pair of first-quarter picks, off which Notre Dame scored 14 points to go up 21-7. The first of those turnovers resulted from a Boubacar Traore hit, and the second one came on a deep throw that safety Luke Talich tracked and snatched after it hung in the air downfield.

Edwards hooked up with wide receiver Jordan Shipp on seven occasions for 109 yards. Tight end Jelani Thurman reeled in five passes, two for touchdowns, and ended the day with 50 receiving yards.

Thurman's second score arrived in garbage time, cutting into UNC's deficit prior to game's end.

articles.title: Pitt QB Mason Heintschel reportedly suffered torn right ACL in win over Virginia Tech
articles.summary: Heintschel threw for 14 TDs over Pitt's first five games of the season.
articles.body:
Pitt is set to enter the AP Top 25 on Sunday. However, the Panthers are going to be without their starting QB for the rest of the season.

According to ESPN , Heintschel suffered a torn ACL in his right knee during the second half of the Panthers' 35-33 win over Virginia Tech on Friday night . Heintschel was injured when he slid toward the sideline and was hit at the same time. He immediately grabbed his knee and was unable to put any weight on his right leg as he was helped to the locker room.

Heintschel later returned to the sideline in street clothes with the assistance of crutches. He was replaced by former Auburn and Texas State quarterback Holden Geriner. The 26 passes Geriner has thrown so far in 2026 are more than he'd thrown in the first four years of his college career combined.

Heintschel was 10-of-18 passing for 113 yards and a TD before he injured his knee. His season ends as he's 98-of-148 passing for 1,304 yards and 14 TDs with just one interception through five games.

He set the ACC record for TD passes in a game with seven in Pitt's season-opening win over Miami (Ohio). While that number was an ACC record, it simply tied a school record. Pete Gonzalez threw for seven TDs in 1997 when Pitt was a member of the Big East.

Pitt beat Virginia Tech as Hokies kicker John Love narrowly missed a game-winning field goal as time expired. Love's kick appeared to either go over or just past wide of the left upright. The ball has to be entirely through the uprights to be considered a make.

The win pushed Pitt to 5-0 and dropped Virginia Tech to 4-1. The Panthers have games against North Carolina and Boston College before heading to No. 4 Miami on Oct. 24.

articles.title: Mason Heintschel injury update: Pitt QB suffers torn ACL, out for season
articles.summary: Pittsburgh quarterback Mason Heintschel suffered a torn ACL, ending his 2026 season in a tough blow for the Panthers.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh quarterback suffered a torn ACL in the Panthers ' win over Virginia Tech on Friday, Oct. 2. ESPN reported , a devastating injury for the undefeated team.

The injury happened early in the third quarter. He scrambled on a play and was near the sideline when he was tackled by two Virginia Tech defenders. Heintschel stayed down on the ground for an extended length of time and was taken to the locker room with his arms around two members of Pitt's medical staff.

He missed the remainder of the game as the Panthers won 35-33.

What Mason Heintschel injury means for Pitt

It's an unfortunate one for Pitt as the sophomore quarterback has been extremely productive this season. In five games, he has thrown for 1,304 yards − sixth most in FBS − and 14 touchdowns − tied for most in the country − with just one interception.

He was a major reason why the Panthers were averaging 38.4 points per game, ranked 30th in FBS.

With the win over Virginia Tech, Pittsburgh moved to 5-0 for the second time in the past three seasons. The Panthers have risen to become an ACC contender, and certainly seemed like they could be in the College Football Playoff conversation given the only ranked game it has left on the schedule is at Miami on Oct. 24. There's also a late season road contest against Louisville on Nov. 21.

Without Heintschel, the Panthers' conference title and playoff hopes take a hit and questions will arise if they can sustain the scoring without their star player.

After Heintschel's injury, he was replaced by Holden Geriner, who held his own as he went 8-for-12 with 78 yards and one touchdown.

A fifth-year player, Geriner is at his third school of his college career. He spent 2022-24 with Auburn and 2025 with Texas State, playing in a total of 11 games prior to his arrival in Pittsburgh.

articles.title: Croatia 0-7 England: Thumping win reinvigorates Thomas Tuchel's project after World Cup blow - but next Spain test will define progress towards success
articles.summary: England's attack was electric and devastating in huge Nations League win in Croatia; performance best of Thomas Tuchel era and highlights areas of progress; but after World Cup heartache England's prospects of future success on big stage will be judged by Spain away in November
articles.body:
Thomas Tuchel knows England's frustrating, much-criticised semi-final defeat to Argentina at the World Cup will hang over him and his team right through until the Euros in 2028 - and even beyond.

But in Croatia on Saturday, a thumping 7-0 win was a performance and result to reinvigorate Tuchel's England project.

It was a historic scoreline: Croatia's heaviest defeat. No team had scored more than four goals away to them before.

Of course, the Nations League is not the World Cup and this ageing Croatia side, a shadow of their great teams of the past, could not provide an elite examination. But England's "complete" performance, as it was described by manager, players and pundits alike, is something to get behind again.

Last week, the positives against Spain were clouded by defensive mistakes and a clear gap in quality; the win over Czech Republic was distorted by the first-half red card. But this was emphatic.

The front four were electric and devastating. Elliot Anderson and Alex Scott, on his first start, bossed the midfield battle against their far more capped counterparts. There was a horror miss from Mateo Kovacic at 3-0 but Croatia were limited to little else, with England's full-backs far busier creating chances than having to stop them.

"When England are rampaging all over the pitch like this, winning back possession when they have no right to do so, passing forward at every opportunity and finishing ruthlessly, there is no better team in world football to watch," wrote Sky Sports News football correspondent Rob Dorsett from the press box.

It was the best performance of the Tuchel era, and the England boss agreed. "It was a fantastic victory. It's an outstanding result, of course, and the performance underlying this result is just on the highest level, from the first minutes to the last," he said.

"The speed and the technical quality today and the hunger off the ball was on the very highest level."

When Tuchel named his squad for this international break, he used his first press conference since the World Cup to insist on the message that this summer's tournament would increase his team's chances of success in the future. The "brotherhood" they built and experiences they shared in North America would be crucial in the next chapter, he explained.

That assessment will have been difficult to swallow for many England fans at the time, with Tuchel's tactical decisions late on against Argentina and his subsequent criticism of English footballers' "DNA" still raw. But perhaps in Rijeka there were signs of that theory starting to play out.

"I just believe we have now a lot of experience together," said Tuchel, when asked why it had clicked in Croatia.

"We had a qualifying campaign together, we had a big tournament together, we have big positive emotions together, we lived through them together, we had big pain together. We just get to know each other better, know the players better and know what to demand and how to motivate.

"It was a good spirit from the start of the camp and it's nice to see that it builds up. It was a day where every puzzle piece fell into place."

Tuchel warned that Czech Republic will provide a different test at Wembley on Tuesday and suggested England fans shouldn't demand seven goals and floods of chances in every game. But they have reasons to expect excitement in that next Nations League game now. A 7-0 win does that.

Spain away on November 15, however, will have a far more powerful impact on the feeling about Tuchel's England and whether the idea they are on a progressive path to glory is correct.

England may well have secured their place in the Nations League quarter-finals by that final group game, with Croatia at home in the days before it. But facing the world champions in Madrid is the kind of test where England must really show how far they have come - and whether they have learned the lessons of the past.

That game will set the tone and feeling over the winter months about whether England are able to go and win on the biggest stages.

For now, this 7-0 thrashing of Croatia, in a small stadium filled with schoolchildren, will provide a welcome uplift.

articles.title: Manchester United Identify This Premier League Defender As A Target: Should Carrick Move In For Him?
articles.summary: Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast, journalist Pete O’Rourke stated that Manchester United have identified Nottingham Forest defender Murillo as a targ...
articles.body:
Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast , journalist Pete O'Rourke stated that Manchester United have identified Nottingham Forest defender Murillo as a target for next year. O'Rourke said

"Murillo has been a previous target for Manchester United because of how well he's done for Nottingham Forest in the Premier League.

"It looks like he is going to be high on their list again because they do want to strengthen in his position, and he is somebody they are very much aware of.

"It'll be a really difficult deal to do because he only signed a new long-term deal last May to keep him at the City Ground until 2030.

"I can't see anything happening in January because Forest don't need the money at the moment and he's a very important player for them.

"So they are ready to put a big price tag on Murillo's head because of his contract situation at the City Ground, and it would take a huge offer if they were to consider letting him go."

Murillo's Impressive Form In The Premier League

Murillo enjoyed a good run of form at the Midlands club in the previous campaign when he put in a series of impressive displays for them on the defensive end of the field. The Brazilian talent made 39 appearances for Nottingham last season, scoring two goals in multiple competitions.

The 24-year-old is currently among the most talented centre-backs in Premier League football. Hence, it is no wonder that the Red Devils are eyeing a move for him next year.

PORTO, PORTUGAL – APRIL 09: Murillo of Nottingham Forest runs with the ball while under pressure from Terem Moffi of FC Porto during the UEFA Europa League 2025/26 Quarter-Final Leg One match between FC Porto and Nottingham Forest FC at Estadio do Dragao on April 09, 2026 in Porto, Portugal. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images)

His current contract at the City Ground will run out in the summer of 2030, which could make it tough for Man United to sign him on the cheap in 2027.

Should Manchester United Boss Michael Carrick Move In For Murillo?

Murillo is a solid tackler of the ball and can scan the danger well to earn possession back for his team inside his half. He usually puts his foot through the ball when needed and excels at playing his way out from the back.

Standing at 1.83m, the Brazilian sensation is a strong presence in the air as well. He has a wealth of experience in the Premier League and won't take any time to adjust to life at Old Trafford.

Murillo would add more bite and steel to Man United boss Michael Carrick's defence. He has what it takes to fight for regular first-team football at the Theatre of Dreams.

At 24, Murillo will only improve with each season. Thus, it makes sense for Carrick to move in for him in the January transfer window or next summer.

articles.title: Santi Denia: "¿El gol anulado? Respeto siempre a los árbitros"
articles.standfirst: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador de la República Checa
articles.summary: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador de la República Checa
articles.body: Santi Denia ha sido el primer entrenador español en enfrentarse a España en un partido de fase de clasificación. El técnico de la República Checa acaba de pasar por la sala de prensa del Carlos Tartiere para analizar lo vivido. Y el polémico gol anulado a su equipo que era el 2-2. El partido: "Estamos muy orgullosos del trabajo. Los jugadores lo han dado todo. Este es el camino" El gol: "Respeto al árbitro. Es un trabajo muy complicado. No me gusta hablar de ellos. Me ha dicho Pablo que ha pitado una falta previa. En el partido, con los nervios, protestas. Nada más". El proceso: "Estamos encantados con el trabajo y rendimiento del equipo. Slama está creciendo. El compromiso es lo más importante. Es el mejor momento para crecer como equipos. Esta experiencia dura de la Nations nos va a servir para el futuro. Hay que mejorar, yo el primero". Sensaciones: "No ha habido tiempo para muchas cosas. Conozco a todo el mundo en la Federación y sé lo que ha crecido. En el abrazo con Luis es el de una amistad de 12 años en el que hubo momentos muy duros. Esto es una luna de miel que tenéis que aprovechar todos".

articles.title: No jugó como nunca pero ganó como siempre
articles.standfirst: La opinión de José Vicente Hernáez
articles.summary: La opinión de José Vicente Hernáez
articles.body: Tenía toda la pinta este partido de terminar con una goleada por todo lo alto, quizá porque los checos son, en teoría al menos, los más flojos del grupo. Además, Lamine Yamal volvió a meter una canasta de tres, de esas que tanto le gustan y que tanto prodiga, es decir, con un disparo a la escuadra desde el borde del área, y la selección española abrió el marcador cuando los checos ni siquiera habían empezado a sudar la camiseta. Seis minutos escasos de juego habían transcurrido, pero ya se barruntaba que los chicos de Luis de la Fuente no estaban por la labor de apretar el acelerador, probablemente porque les espera un partido en Croacia el martes próximo. Y tras el gol de Rodri, que suele meter pocos (aunque un gol suyo le dio al Manchester City su única Champions League), incluso parecía que se le había acabado la gasolina y estaba circulando con la reserva encendida. En la segunda parte estuvo a punto de suceder lo que nadie esperaba. La selección española seguía jugando al tran-tran y los checos aprovecharon para hacer un gol en un buen contragolpe. Y hasta pudo empatar en un error de David Raya, al que se le escapó un balón que debió despejar a córner en vez de blocarlo, pero el árbitro pitó una falta y anuló el gol. No habría sido justo ese posible 2-2, que conste. Que no jugase la selección como debía y como suele hacerlo no significa que no mereciese la victoria. Y es que hasta no jugando bien es superior a sus rivales. Para resumir lo que fue este partido: España no jugó como nunca, pero ganó como siempre... porque fue mejor. Se le aclaró el panorama cuando los checos se quedaron con uno menos y al final tuvo que ser Merino, cómo no, el que dictó sentencia como suele ser habitual en él, es decir, cuando el árbitro está a punto de pitar el final.

articles.title: De la Fuente: "Es difícil mantener el equilibrio entre resultados y la salud de los jugadores"
articles.standfirst: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador español
articles.summary: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador español
articles.body: La sala de prensa del Real Oviedo acaba de acoger a Luis de la Fuente para que el seleccionador español ofreciera sus impresiones del duelo ante la República Checa. Partido: "La lectura es esa. El primer tiempo ha sido muy bueno. En el segundo, los cambios no ayudan y no hemos dado continuidad al juego. La exigencia es tremenda con ese calendario. Hemos perdido finura. No estamos contentos porque hubo momentos en los que hemos sufrido mucho y no estamos acostumbrados". Rotaciones y calendario: "Es difícil mantener el equilibrio resultados-salud de los jugadores. Hacemos lo que podemos. Los partidos hay que ganarlos, pero lo principal es la salud. A ver si no hay más lesiones. Seguro que de aquí al martes alguno va a notar más el cansancio. Los rivale tamnbién". Croacia: "No es normal el 0-7. Tenemos que ver qué ha pasado, porquezes muy extraño. Eso hará que salgan mucho más motivados, porque para jugadores de ese nivel no encajan algo sí con facilidad" Lamine: "Su crecimiento es una realidad diaria. articles.title: Jeremiah Smith Makes Ohio State History, Gets LeBron Shoutout After Breaking Olave's TD Record
articles.summary: Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith made history during the No. 5 Buckeyes' matchup with No. 14 Iowa on Saturday.
articles.body:
Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith made history during the No. 5 Buckeyes' matchup with No. 14 Iowa on Saturday.

Smith recorded his 36th career receiving touchdown in the third quarter of the contest, breaking Ohio State's all-time record.

Caitlin Clark to appear on College GameDay

He received a shoutout from LeBron James, a noted Ohio State fan, for the accomplishment.

The Buckeyes' previous record for all-time receiving touchdowns was set by Chris Olave during the 2021 season.

It's worth noting that Olave recorded his 35th touchdown catch near the end of his fourth year at Ohio State, while Smith is in the middle of his third season with the Buckeyes.

Smith wasn't finished writing his name into the Buckeyes' history books on Saturday, as he also set their all-time receptions record in the third quarter against the Hawkeyes.

The 20-year-old sits atop Ohio State's all-time receiving yards list as well after setting the new record on Sept. 19.

Smith was already a top weapon in the Buckeyes' passing attack from 2024-25, but he's established himself as a true threat to win the Heisman Trophy this season.

In his first four games of the year, he reeled in 33 catches for 617 yards and seven touchdowns.

Smith didn't show any signs of slowing down against Iowa, recording six receptions for 111 yards in the first half.

articles.title: North Macedonia 0-2 Scotland: Two going on four, five or six on good night for new era
articles.summary: Scotland scored twice in North Macedonia but the scoreline does not reflect their dominance in Skopje, writes Tom English.
articles.body:
When Scott McKenna was sent off late in the night in Skopje, North Macedonia did something they looked entirely incapable of doing for 80-plus minutes spent buried in Scotland's collective pocket.

They strung a couple of passes together, had a few shots, raised an odd cheer from their dismally small support.

Fair play to them because for much of this Nations League game it looked as if they were comatose; out-played and out-fought. Scotland, with their energy and urgency, had reduced them to the ranks of the lifeless.

Skopje is a city of statues, two or three hundred of them apparently, great big things in squares and in fountains commemorating tsars and dames, emperors and warriors, royalty and revolutionaries.

You could have taken any 11 of them off their perch and put them in the North Macedonia starting line-up and they'd have posed Scotland more of a challenge than the beleaguered home team managed for most of this encounter.

At one point in the first half a dog ran on to the pitch. They'd have been better off putting a shirt on his back. At least he'd have had some bite.

Scotland beat North Macedonia in Nations League for Pocognoli's first win

'It means everything' - numbers behind Robertson's 100-cap Scotland career

Robertson hits 100 Scotland caps - but who else makes top 10?

The scoreline does a terrible job in capturing what happened.

Scotland had 25 shots to nine, 10 on target to zero. Before McKenna walked, they had touched the ball 37 times in North Macedonia's penalty area, North Macedonia had touched it twice in Scotland's.

On the night that Andy Robertson won his 100th cap, this was one of his most straightforward matches of all. A stroll. A rout, if two goals can be called a rout.

Two going on four and five, maybe six on what was a poor pitch in a soulless stadium, save for the visiting fans, who made a racket, as ever. It was a good evening for the new era.

Scotland were exciting, entertaining and also frustrating. They had ambition but not enough execution. They created chance upon chance but didn't have the killer touch nearly as often as you'd like. That might come as things progress.

Certainly, a burden was lifted off the head coach, Sebastien Pocognoli. No more chat about the search for the elusive goal, no more of that creeping negativity as he waited for a first win. The air is a touch lighter for him now as he prepares for Slovenia at Hampden on Tuesday.

It was a big occasion for Robertson the centurion; a major achievement in the career of Kieron Bowie, who rifled in a terrific early goal that settled everyone down; a memorable experience for Luis Binks, Stephen Welsh and the substitute Robbie Ure, who now know what it feels like not just to play for their country but to win for their country. Binks and Welsh look at home in that Scotland defence.

There was a strong sense from the start that everything would be OK for Scotland and it came in the shape of the Duracell Bunny that was the captain.

Robertson began like a dervish. A shot after five minutes, then another and another and another. Four shots in 13 minutes - he's never had four shots in 90 minutes in any one of his 99 caps before Saturday.

There was positivity for Scotland from early on.

They had six shots in 15 minutes, the most picture-perfect of them being Bowie's strike. Oli McBurnie did some work beforehand - his wait for a goal goes on, 19 caps and counting - then the wonderful Billy Gilmour got involved.

Is Gilmour a six or an eight? The truth is that he's both, a tempo-setter when dropping deep, a dangerous passer when moving forward, a complete footballer at the peak of his powers.

Then it was all about Bowie. His footwork did for a defender, his accuracy did for a goalkeeper. It was a rare moment of precision in front of goal, another illustration that despite their issues in scoring goals, Scotland have a promising array of strikers these days. Time, and the confidence of this victory, should make them better.

Ben Gannon-Doak turned North Macedonia inside out and upside down. He is woefully short of minutes for his club, Bournemouth, and lacks sharpness and ruthlessness as a consequence. His delivery has always lacked accuracy.

His raw materials, though, are exhilarating. His pace, his involvement, his number of touches, his chances.

He never left North Macedonia alone. They survived only because he blasted over with one of his chances, shot tamely with another, lost composure with a third one. Having tormented North Macedonia, he allowed them off the hook, but he was a one-man thrill-fest.

He's 20, that can't be forgotten. He's going to be around for a lot of years and will play a heap of big games, but with his club he's got some decisions to make.

Two minutes against Liverpool, 19 against Sociedad, eight against Brentford, one minute against Newcastle and Man City. The only game he has started this season was a League Cup tie against Lincoln.

Bournemouth is a tough team to get into, but he needs more time on the grass, more opportunity to develop. Maybe a loan move in January would make sense for him, if his club allows him to go. A big 'if'.

That's a situation Gannon-Doak needs to resolve for himself - and for Scotland.

The chances flowed - one thunderbolt from the influential John McGinn, one near-miss from Bowie after excellence from Gannon-Doak, one off a post from McKenna.

A second came via the penalty. McGinn lashed it home and drew alongside Lawrie Reilly on the all-time list - 22 and counting.

After some indifferent performances, that one would have meant an awful lot to him, a strike to silence some mild questioning of his impact, a goal to put the confidence back in him, if it ever left.

Pocognoli has something to build on now, three points to go with that strong second half against Slovenia a week ago; new players, aggressive football, a bit of buzz. North Macedonia were hopeless but it hardly matters. They were put away comfortably.

In this series of footballing sprints, there's just one of the original four games to go now - Tuesday at Hampden. Promising signs but so much still left to do.

articles.title: Jeremiah Smith, Sayin's Box Score Stats, Highlights, Heisman Hype from Ohio State vs. Iowa
articles.summary: If there was any doubt about who the most dominant player in college football is right now, Jeremiah Smith put the argument to rest on Saturday with another historic outing in Ohio State's 31-14 win over Iowa.
articles.body:
If there was any doubt about who the most dominant player in college football is right now, Jeremiah Smith put the argument to rest on Saturday with another historic outing in Ohio State's 31-14 win over Iowa.

Smith, who entered the day leading FBS in receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, added 206 yards and two touchdowns to his season total to help the Buckeyes win.

Ohio State came into the game favored by 14.5 points on the road, per FanDuel Sportsbook . It was able to cover the spread by scoring 21 unanswered points at one period from the second through fourth quarters.

Two weeks after setting the Ohio State record for receiving yards, Smith became the school's all-time leader in receptions and receiving touchdowns on Saturday.

The touchdown record came on Smith's second score of the day from 57 yards in the third quarter.

Smith's receptions record was on a much less dramatic play, but still a historic moment in a career already full of them.

Smith's performance moved him into the top spot in the latest Heisman odds at +115 (bet $100 to win $115) from FanDuel.

The feeling about Smith's Heisman candidacy was very strong among those who were watching him play against the Hawkeyes.

It's hard to come up with new superlatives to describe Smith since he has been doing this for three seasons now, though the results through five games in 2026 might be on another level.

Smith has surpassed the 200-yard mark in back-to-back games. His worst game of the season was against Kent State with 85 yards on five catches when he basically didn't have to play in the second half because it was 35-0 at halftime.

Taking out that game, Smith's lowest receiving yardage total in the other four contests is 151 yards against Ball State. His 823 receiving yards are more than UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava has passing (820) entering play on Saturday.

Given how dominant Smith has been, it's hard to separate how much of Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin's success this year is a product of his growth or playing alongside the best player in college football.

Sayin is now up to 1,530 passing yards, 13 touchdowns and one interception with a 72.5 completion percentage through five games.

There's no doubt Smith is the straw stirring the drink for Ohio State. Sayin's development will go a long way toward ensuring the Buckeyes remain a factor in the playoff race as their margin of error narrowed following the loss to Texas.

Saturday was the Buckeyes' first big test since that Sept. 12 defeat, as they were on the road against an undefeated Big Ten opponent. They looked a little sluggish early before finally pulling away.

Ohio State gets to return home next week to host Maryland before a showdown against No. 6 Indiana in Bloomington on Oct. 10. The Hoosiers defeated OSU in the Big Ten Championship Game last season en route to winning a national title.

articles.title: CFB Playoff Picture, Standings and Bracket Predictions After Week 5 of 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: The Florida Gators became the latest College Football Playoff contender to learn how difficult life can be on the road in the SEC.
articles.body:
The Florida Gators became the latest College Football Playoff contender to learn how difficult life can be on the road in the SEC.

Florida was outclassed across the board by the Missouri Tigers in the most significant result of Week 5.

The eighth-ranked Gators, who pulled off a top-10 upset of their own at home last week, were the only top-10 team to lose in the afternoon windows on Saturday.

The Ohio State Buckeyes and Alabama Crimson Tide were among the top-10 teams who were far more fortunate on their travels on Saturday.

Ohio State began its five-week Big Ten gauntlet with a commanding win over the Iowa Hawkeyes.

The bracket projection is based on the latest rankings and Week 5 results.

No. 8 Florida Falls On the Road At Missouri

Florida didn't have much time to celebrate its first big win under Jon Sumrall.

The Gators suffered a 45-17 defeat at the hands of Missouri one week after they defeated the Ole Miss Rebels in Gainesville.

Florida experienced a 13-position swing upward in the AP Top 25 after its Week 4 win. A similar swing in the other direction is expected on Sunday.

Saturday's loss is massive in the context of Florida's case to make the CFB Playoff.

Florida still has to play the top-ranked Texas Longhorns and the No. 2 Georgia Bulldogs in consecutive games at the end of the month.

The margin for error is incredibly small with the Gators and there's now a chance they end up outside the Top 25 by the end of the month.

No. 5 Ohio State Begins Big Ten Gauntlet With Road Win Over Iowa

Jeremiah Smith and the Ohio State Buckeyes had zero issues in Iowa City on Saturday.

The Buckeyes produced a 31-14 win over the Iowa Hawkeyes, who came into Saturday inside the top 15.

The trip to Iowa marked the start of four Top 20 opponents over a five-game span for Ohio State.

Smith strengthened his Heisman Trophy case with 206 receiving yards and a pair of touchdown catches.

Ohio State will need Smith to perform at a high level in the coming weeks to get past the Indiana Hoosiers, Oregon Ducks and USC Trojans.

The expectation is for Ohio State to go at least 2-1 in that stretch to maintain a good position in the CFB Playoff race.

If they perform at Saturday's level, Ohio State might go undefeated through its tough schedule and reside in a great position to even contend for a first-round bye come mid-November.

articles.title: No. 25 Missouri spoils No. 8 Florida's brief time near the top of the AP poll with a dominant 45-17 win
articles.summary: The Tigers scored 35 straight points in the blowout.
articles.body:
Florida's time in the top 10 lasted exactly one week.

The Gators vaulted up 13 spots to No. 8 in the AP Top 25 after a blowout win over Ole Miss in Week 4. Now, the Gators are going to find themselves tumbling down the rankings on Sunday after a 45-17 loss at No. 25 Missouri.

It's a massive win for a Mizzou program that has struggled against top-tier competition under coach Eli Drinkwitz. Outside of bowl games, the Tigers entered the game just 6-19 against ranked opponents in Drinkwitz's tenure. And it had been 13 years since Missouri got a regular-season win over a top-10 opponent.

A week ago, Florida ran all over Ole Miss. On Saturday, Missouri ran all over Florida in the second half as Jamal Roberts put the game away with a pair of massive runs.

With the Tigers leading by 20, Roberts broke off a hide-and-seek 77-yard run to set up a TD and a 28-point lead.

And then on the first play of Missouri's next possession, Roberts made it a five-touchdown game with an 80-yard score.

Before those two runs, Roberts had run for just 44 yards on 17 carries as Missouri had picked apart Florida's defense through the air. QB Austin Simmons was 23-of-30 passing for 340 yards and two first-half touchdowns. The first was a 47-yard strike to Donovan Olugbode. The second was a 36-yard TD to Caleb Goodie with 2:05 to go before halftime.

Florida tied the game at 10-10 with 4:26 to go in the second quarter. By the time there was 12:24 to go in the third quarter, the Gators trailed 27-10.

That seven-minute sequence was a perfect encapsulation of how the game started to unravel for the Gators. RB Jadan Baugh never looked like himself on Saturday and ended up with just 12 carries for 13 yards. Twelve of those yards came on one run. Missouri's defensive line and linebackers consistently pushed the Florida offensive line into the backfield.

That put more pressure on QB Aaron Philo, especially with leading receiver Vernell Brown III out. Philo didn't play especially poorly; but as the win over Ole Miss showed, the Florida offense is operating far better with a run game that's consistently getting chunk yardage.

Florida finished the game with just 42 yards rushing, and a significant portion of that yardage came late in the fourth quarter with the game out of reach.

It was a stark reminder that early-season climbs can be followed by drops that are just as precipitous. And also proof that Jon Sumrall's Florida turnaround probably needs more than a few weeks. The Gators host South Carolina in Week 6 before games against No. 1 Texas and No. 2 Georgia to end October.

The Tigers lost at Mississippi State in Week 4 after giving up 14 unanswered points in the fourth quarter. With the Bulldogs getting blitzed at home earlier in the day by No. 7 Alabama, it's fair to say that no result is going to be a surprise among the teams that currently occupy the second tier of the SEC.

Mizzou can safely consider itself a member of that group, especially when Simmons is throwing the ball as well as he has so far in 2026. The Ole Miss transfer is the most dynamic passer the Tigers have had in years and gives the Missouri offense an ability to beat teams deep on any given play that it simply hasn't had in recent seasons.

It's an offensive aspect that's sorely needed as it looks less and less likely that Ahmad Hardy will return to the lineup anytime soon after suffering a gunshot wound in his leg in the spring. The All-American back was the source of Missouri's explosiveness in 2025 as he rushed for 1,649 yards and 16 scores.

Roberts is now the focal point of the Mizzou rushing attack in Hardy's absence after rushing for over 750 yards on 124 carries in 2025. Can he and Simmons push Mizzou further toward the top of the conference?

Conversations about Florida being a potential contender this season lasted about one week.

The Missouri Tigers absolutely dominated the Gators on Saturday, blowing them out 45-17 behind a passing game that moved the ball at will all evening and an epic performance from running back Jamal Roberts.

Here's a look at the game's key performers:

As lopsided as the final score was, it doesn't quite put into perspective just how one-sided this game was (especially after halftime). And after Florida tied the game at 10-apiece in the second quarter, Missouri rattled off 35 straight points until Florida finally pushed across one final touchdown in the fourth quarter.

The Gators will have to recovery quickly, as a winnable matchup next weekend against South Carolina is followed by a road game at Texas and a home game against Georgia to close out October.

As for Missouri, the Tigers will assuredly be the newest SEC flavor of the week and will be bumped up the rankings. They'll look to avoid a similar letdown to the one that befell Florida when they face Texas A&M next week.

articles.title: B/R's 2025 College Football Winners and Losers from Week 5
articles.summary: We're in October now and thank goodness for that. With kinder weather comes enormous college football stakes.
articles.body:
We're in October now and thank goodness for that. With kinder weather comes enormous college football stakes.

It wasn't just Saturday, either. Friday night gave us plenty to digest, and the action on Saturday never relinquished. We saw one Heisman campaign hit an enormous bump in the road, while an unlikely conference broke in its new stadium in emphatic fashion.

There's plenty to unpack, and unpack we shall. As these games unfold, we will continue to update with every detail of the day.

It was supposed to be different at Virginia Tech. That has largely been the case through the first four weeks of the season, albeit against a favorable schedule.

But on Friday night, James Franklin's fresh start endured some familiar pain as the Hokies fell at home to Pittsburgh.

This one had multiple pieces of disappointment worth unpacking. For starters, Virginia Tech was up 14-0 after less than five minutes, and the route looked to be on. Then there's the fact that Pitt starting QB Mason Heintschel, who has been one of the nation's best QBs early on, was knocked out of the game with an injury.

Finally, and most painful of all, Tech's potential game-winning field goal at the end of game, which appeared to sail just left the goal post, might have actually been good upon further viewings. It's a play likely to be discussed for days to follow.

Regardless, Pitt was deemed victorious 35-33 and all Franklin could do is give kicker John Love and move on. Given Franklin's big moment struggles at Penn State, the scene was oddly familiar.

What does $875 million buy you in the year 2026? How about a sparkling new college football stadium?

On Friday night, Northwestern debuted its new Ryan Field, a 35,000-seat, state-of-the-art masterpiece. And the debut game couldn't have gone much better.

With Chip Kelly calling plays, the Wildcats tallied more than 506 yards of offense against Penn State. Perhaps more astonishingly is that 413 of those yards came on the ground. The end result was a 34-13 thrashing of the Nittany Lions.

For Penn State, the questions and concerns are real. For Northwestern, which recently gave head coach David Braun an extension, this moment could serve as a warning to future Big Ten opponents.

The Wildcats, which gave Indiana a game a few weeks ago, still play Oregon, Ohio State and Iowa. And if the offense can run the ball like this, this team should remain a factor in the conference.

What a night. What a debut. That's how you open up a stadium.

To be clear, Kamario Taylor still delivered more than his fair share of dazzling throws in the 56-23 loss to Alabama.

Even on a day when he wasn't at his best—and perhaps not 100 percent healthy coming in—Mississippi State's QB still showcased why the football world is so excited about his future. He also still accounted for three touchdowns.

But three turnovers, including a fumble and a pick-six early on, put his team in a difficult spot from the start. The Bulldogs tried to keep the game close, although things got out of hand in the second half. And when it did, Taylor came out of the game with an apparent injury.

Given his performance through September, Taylor was receiving plenty of Heisman buzz and for good reason. While this loss doesn't remove him from the discussion, it's an enormous setback.

Perhaps more concerning on that front is what is still to come. Mississippi State still has road games at LSU, Texas and Ole Miss on tap. There will be plenty of chances to make a Heisman impression, although it'll be an uphill climb from here on out.

Expert CFB Locks for Week 5's Biggest Games 🔒

It starts with quarterback Keelon Russell. Of course it does.

Making just his fifth start, Russell looked like the best quarterback in college football and a future Heisman finalist. For as sensational as he's been, however, the rest of Alabama's offense deserves an enormous amount of praise as well for the 56-23 win.

Last season, the running game was broken. Against Mississippi State, it looked very much alive and largely provided the change of pace this team lacked in 2025.

As for the wide receivers, they were sensational. Lotzeir Brooks, Rico Scott, Marshall Pritchett and Ryan Coleman-Williams all showed flashes, regularly making contested, meaningful catches that derailed any chance of a Mississippi State comeback.

Alabama finished with 56 points and 485 yards, and it could have been much more. The Crimson Tide essentially ran the clock out for the last 15 minutes of the game.

What a performance. And what timing with Georgia coming to town next week.

Loser: Florida's College Football Playoff Chances

As if we needed another reminder, this sport moves quickly.

One week, you're the darling. The next, you're on the wrong side of a blowout.

The fact that we're talking about Florida's College Football Playoff resume speaking to the sensational work head coach Jon Sumrall has done in Gainesville. This program is clearly better, as it showcased in a dominating win over Ole Miss in Week 4.

But as we saw in Week 5, there still is work to do.

Missouri didn't just beat Florida; the Tigers dominated the Gators 45-17. Quarterback Austin Simmons carved up the Gators, making it look easy at times. And the Florida offense simply couldn't keep up.

One week after falling to Ole Miss, Missouri responded in a major way.

In time, we'll know exactly what it means for Florida. There's plenty of time—and ample spotlight games—to turn things around. Sumrall's team plays Texas and Georgia in a few weeks.

A week ago, in the aftermath of Minnesota's win over Washington, P.J. Fleck wiped the blood of linebacker Maverick Baranowski on his cheek, in a moment that went understandably viral.

Prior to his team's game against Michigan on Saturday, Fleck was seen crowd surfing during the pregame. Then his team pulled off a massive 20-14 upset over Michigan, the team's second outright win as an underdog in a row.

Fleck in true Fleck fashion couldn't help himself.

"I couldn't be prouder," Fleck screamed . "Besides my marriage and my kids being born, this might be the best day of my life."

At the very least, Fleck isn't boring. His style is undoubtedly unique, although he's never been shy about doing it his own way.

And at 4-1, with winnable games on the horizon, this likely isn't the last we've heard from him. Stay tuned.

At some point, declaring Jeremiah Smith the Heisman favorite isn't enough.

Ohio State's star wideout, fresh off a 11-catch, 206-yard, two-touchdown performance against Iowa, demands something greater. The Buckeyes dominated Iowa 31-14, thanks in large part to Smith.

Best college football wide receiver ever? We have to start talking about it.

Through five games, Smith has nine touchdown receptions. He's gone over 150 receiving yards in all but one game. For further context, his 85-yard receiving performance against Kent State was limited largely because his playing time was limited in a blowout.

We've reached the point of absurdity that it's hard to quantify exactly what we're seeing.

Each week, it becomes easier to compare him to Julio Jones, Calvin Johnson and the other all-time collegiate wideouts that made the sport look easy. Smith is there, and he has the opportunity to deliver one of the all-time great seasons the position has ever seen.

Coming into Saturday, Maryland's Mike Locksley and South Carolina's Shane Beamer were two coaches most in need of wins to cool the dreaded hot seat chatter.

Leaving Saturday, Locksley and Beamer need miracles to save their jobs. In fact, we might be past the point of miracles.

Both teams jumped out to early double-digit leads. Both teams coughed up those leads shortly after. Maryland lost to Nebraska 48-23; South Carolina lost to Kentucky 35-24 in overtime, which was gutting given the recent drama surrounding the Gamecocks.

The Terrapins are 2-3 with a game at Ohio State looming. Needless to say, that could be ugly. The Gamecocks are also 2-3, with games at Florida and against Tennessee coming up next. That same thought applies.

At this point, both jobs seem destined to open up. It's simply a matter of when.

articles.title: Who is Rafa Marquez? Mexico head coach returns to USMNT rivalry where El Tri boss is hated
articles.summary: As the United States men face off against their CONCACAF rivals Mexico on Saturday in an international friendly, the third of this lengthy window, many USMNT...
articles.body:
As the United States men face off against their CONCACAF rivals Mexico on Saturday in an international friendly, the third of this lengthy window, many USMNT fans will be surprised to recognize the new El Tri head coach.

In the aftermath of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, where Mexico was eliminated in heartbreaking fashion against England in a dogfight at Estadio Azteca, El Tri parted ways with Javier Aguirre, making a change at the helm to begin a new World Cup cycle.

In comes Rafa Marquez, the one-time captain and longtime legend of the Mexican national team. Marquez has a long history leading El Tri on the field, and now he will lead them off it, wearing street clothes on the touchline.

When asked before his first coaching appearance against the United States if he was aware of his villain status in the United States, he had a cheeky response. "I don't know what you're talking about," Marquez said. "I've already forgotten about that." USMNT fans probably haven't, though.

One of the greatest players to ever take the field for Mexico, Rafa Marquez began his career as a young player in the youth system of Liga MX club Atlas, debuting for the club at 17 years old in 1996.

After three seasons with his boyhood club, he was spotted by European scouts at the 1999 Copa America and made the switch to French side Monaco, where he would play four years, making 109 appearances.

After being named to the Ligue 1 Team of the Season in a league title-winning 2002/03 campaign, he got a move to Barcelona in the summer of 2003, joining for just over €5 million. He would become a fixture at the La Liga giants, making 242 appearances for the Catalan side over a seven-year career at the Camp Nou.

During his time there, Marquez would win two UEFA Champions League titles, four La Liga titles, and a host of other trophies. He would play alongside Barcelona greats like Lionel Messi , Lillian Thuram, Eric Abidal, Carles Puyol, Andres Iniesta, Xavi, Ronaldinho, Thierry Henry, Samuel Eto'o, and many others.

Marquez's best season came in the 2005/06 campaign, when he made 25 starts in La Liga play plus another eight in the Champions League, including a full 90-minute performance in the UEFA Champions League final where they beat Arsenal .

When his Barcelona career concluded, Marquez moved to the New York Red Bulls in Major League Soccer, spending three seasons in the United States, winning the Eastern Conference title in 2010 but flopping in the playoffs all three times. His career was far from over though, as Marquez would play well into his late 30's with stints at Club Leon, Italian side Hellas Verona, and then back at Atlas to finish his career.

By his retirement in 2018, he was 39 years old and had made over 600 career appearances on the club side, scoring 26 goals. Marquez would first move into a front office role at Atlas, named the club's new sporting director. He would hold that role for less than a year, departing in May of 2019.

After some time as an analyst for TUDN, he joined the youth ranks at Atlas, where he once came through as a young player himself. In 2022, he was appointed the head coach of Barcelona Atletic, where he would stay for two years, before moving back home to join Javier Aguirre's setup at the Mexican senior national team.

He was hired as head coach to replace Aguirre after the 2026 World Cup, his first senior head coaching job.

As one of the most legendary players in the history of the Mexican national team, Rafa Marquez built a glittering career at the international level.

Overall, Marquez made 148 international appearances, scoring 17 goals. He has the joint-fourth-most appearances in national team history, behind only Andres Guardado (180), Claudio Suarez (178), and Guillermo Ochoa (153) and level with Pavel Pardo.

As a defensive midfielder, and occasionally deputizing as a defender, he was known for his tenacity and grit on the pitch. He holds the Mexico record for most World Cup appearances with 19, and in 2018 became the fourth player to appear at five consecutive World Cup tournaments after Antonio Carbajal, Lothar Matthaus, and Gianluigi Buffon.

Rafa Marquez history vs. USA as a player

Rafa Marquez became known as a massive villain in the United States, mostly during his time with the Mexico national team.

He made his first appearance against the United States in the 1999 Confederations Cup, helping Mexico shut out their rivals in a 1-0 golden-goal victory in the semifinals.

After that, however, Marquez would be known for two infamous moments. First, he was sent off in their World Cup Round of 16 meeting for a bad head-to-head clash with Cobi Jones, with the U.S. already leading 2-0. Then, he was shown another red card for an absolutely awful kung-fu kick to the knee of USMNT goalkeeper Tim Howard in 2009 World Cup qualifying.

He would, however, be part of some big wins against Mexico's main rival too. He would play a big part in multiple World Cup qualifying wins at Estadio Azteca, making the USMNT's life at the famed Mexican arena a living hell. He would score a goal in his final match against the United States, a World Cup qualifier in 2016 that marked the only time Mexico would beat the U.S. on home soil in qualifying during his career.

articles.title: Match review: Royals salvage a point on the road with last minute stunner
articles.summary: Royals secure an ever-important before heading into the FIFA break.
articles.body:
Utah Royals FC battled back to net a goal in the last minute of play, earning a hard-fought 1-1 draw at Lynn Family Stadium Saturday afternoon after conceding late in the first half.

Mozingo's last-second heroics secures point for Royals

The Royals entered the afternoon road match with energy, finding tangible opportunities up the pitch within the first 20 minutes in hopes of taking an early lead to beat Racing Louisville on the road, a feat neither side has accomplished since the Royals return to Utah in 2024 with the respective home side coming out on top in each of the two squads' last five matches.

Veteran playmaker Paige Cronin made her return to the pitch as a halftime substitute, eligible for the first time Saturday since the one-game suspension for the red card she received in the loss to Angel City FC. Cronin immediately brought energy up the right-side of the pitch to help the visitors earn tangible opportunities for the equalizer.

The exciting road battle came down to the final minute as Utah native Brecken Mozingo salvaged a point for the Royals, netting a stoppage time screamer in the sixth and final minute of stoppage time. The score marked her second of the 2026 season and sixth of her professional career.

"Honestly, Brecken is so clinical. That is a big thing she brings, in every single training she will put that shot away," said Cronin. "So as soon as she had it, I was like, 'that's the person we want on top of the box,' and just credit to her for just smacking it. It was so cool." - URFC Veteran Paige Cronin

While the Royals maintained control throughout much of the beginning minutes of the match, the home side nearly took the lead with two chances just moments apart in the 25th minute. Following a corner kick, it was Japanese star and URFC leading scorer Mina Tanaka who impressively stepped up with a goal-line header to keep the home side off the score sheet then, veteran keeper Mandy McGlynn followed suit just seconds later, stopping a head-on shot by Louisville's Emma Sears to deny the home side the opening goal.

In the 42nd minute Racing Louisville converted a penalty following VAR review for a foul in the box to take a 1-0 lead. While the Royals continued to battle throughout the remainder of the first half and the added four minutes of stoppage time by putting relentless pressure on the defense in hopes of the equalizer, the visitors entered the halftime break down by one.

With Cronin on the pitch to begin the second half the Royals came out with energy, working to move the ball up the pitch ultimately earning three early chances on goal by both Tanaka and Spanish defender Nuria Rábano. In the 72nd minute, recently acquired forward Jameese Joseph earned one of the best looks on goal for Utah in just her fourth match with the squad.

The consistent pressure by the visitors paid off in the final minute of stoppage time as Cronin showcased speed and impressive footwork to keep the ball from fully crossing over the goal-line and setting up Mozingo who settled the ball with her body before ripping a powerful shot into the back of the net to secure an ever-important point for the visitors just moments before the final whistle.

The Royals will have a break in play for the FIFA October International Window next week before returning to the Wasatch Front on Saturday, Oct. 17, welcoming the Kansas City Current to America First Field. Kickoff for the match is scheduled for 4:30 p.m. MDT and tickets are available for purchase at rsl.com.

articles.title: Jeremiah Smith makes Heisman statement with latest outing in win over No. 14 Iowa: 'I'm the best player in the country'
articles.summary: Jeremiah Smith has racked up 423 receiving yards and six touchdowns in the past two weeks for the Buckeyes.
articles.body:
IOWA CITY, Iowa — Ryan Day knows he has a problem on his hands when it comes to Jeremiah Smith.

And after the star wide receiver put not only the rest of the Big Ten conference, but everyone else in the Heisman Trophy conversation, on notice Saturday, it's only going to get worse.

"Every coach in America is going to say, 'We've got to take this guy away,'" Day said.

Smith led No. 5 Ohio State to a dominant 31-14 win over No. 14 Iowa on Saturday afternoon, spoiling what was one of the biggest games at Kinnick Stadium in the past two decades. He had 206 yards and two touchdowns on 11 catches in the win, which marked his second consecutive 200-yard outing. Smith had a career-high 217 yards and four touchdowns in the Buckeyes' blowout win over Illinois last week.

Smith broke both the Ohio State receiving touchdowns record and the school's receptions record in the process. He already held the yardage record, so Smith holds all three major categories for a wide receiver in Columbus.

The last two outings are the only times that Smith has surpassed 200 receiving yards in a single game in his career. He also entered Saturday as the nation's leader in receiving yards, and tied for the most in receiving touchdowns.

"I just want more, really," Smith said. "I'm never satisfied."

It's not just the numbers that Smith is putting up that is turning heads. It's how he's doing it.

There was one play on Saturday in which Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin threw into triple coverage, and the ball somehow made it through to Smith. He turned it into a 54-yard gain. Fittingly, that was the 200th catch of his career.

Smith, Day and Sayin all laughed about that after the game, and admitted that the ball should not have been thrown. They got lucky.

"That throw, I didn't expect Julian to throw that one. I was surprised he threw it," Smith said. "But it just shows we have trust in each other, and he expects me to make that play. That's exactly what I'm going to do."

He did it again later, too, making a grab with two defenders — one of them was called for a holding penalty — all over him.

The final touchdown of the day, though, he was wide open.

And once he reached the back of the end zone, Smith hit the Heisman celebration.

"There's times where he's covered, and we still make the throw and catch," Day said. "It just speaks to his ability, and Julian's trust with him. But then there's other plays where he was open … The only way that that works is if he practices the way he does to work through all the issues and timing that comes with it and all the basics. I can't say enough about who he is as a person."

Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz quickly compared him to Philadelphia Eagles star and former Penn State standout Saquon Barkley in terms of how dominant he is as a player.

"We gave him everything we had, and he's still pretty effective. … All you can do is do your best and try to be as smart as you can playing him," Ferentz said. "He's a great player.

"With a little bit of luck, we won't see him again in my career."

Ohio State now sits at 4-1 after Saturday's win. The Buckeyes will take on Maryland at home next weekend before a tough three-game stretch that includes road games at No. 6 Indiana and No. 18 USC, and a home battle with No. 15 Oregon.

All three of those opponents are sure to try and find different ways to at least slow Smith down, something that's been just about impossible so far this fall. The only game in which he's been held below 150 receiving yards this season was their blowout 59-3 win over Kent State.

Though the team's conference title and postseason aspirations are very real, Smith has something else on his mind, too. And after Saturday, he's now likely out in front in that race.

"I just gotta keep the Heisman voters, or whoever it is, [aware] that I'm the best player in the country," he said plainly.

articles.title: Rhode Island football wins Governor's Cup in nail-biter against Brown
articles.summary: Brown had all the momentum, until Ty Groff's 43-yard field goal with 11 seconds sealed the win for URI at Centreville Bank Stadium on Oct. 3, 2026.
articles.body:
PAWTUCKET – Ty Groff had a feeling he might get one last chance, and the University of Rhode Island kicker made the most of it.

His second 43-yard field goal on this Saturday afternoon came with 11 seconds to play, and it returned the Governor's Cup to the Rams after a year-long absence.

Brown missed out on a golden opportunity to win consecutive games in this rivalry for the first time in a decade. It was URI celebrating under the sunshine at Centreville Bank Stadium thanks to this 13-10 squirmer.

The Rams punted with 1:19 left to pin the Bears inside their own 20 and used their defense to record a quick three-and-out. URI started in prime field position at the Brown 46 with 32 seconds left and benefited from a personal foul that brought the ball within Groff's range. His line-drive kick sailed through the uprights, and the Rams hoisted the silver trophy at midfield, courtesy of Gov. Dan McKee.

"I would say it's just trusting myself," Groff said. "I've had a lot of ups and downs in my life, whether it was high school or college. It's all about belief."

URI had possession in a 10-10 game earlier in the fourth quarter and moved the ball across midfield before facing a second fourth down on the drive. The Rams elected to kick it away, and Randy Leavitt dropped one softly to the Bears 12. Brown gained two yards on a Matt Childs rush and threw a pair of incomplete passes – Andre DePina-Gray deflected the second one in the backfield to force a Bears punt.

"I just couldn't be more proud of everybody," URI coach Jim Fleming said. "That's what every coach says, but our kids had a resolve today. They were not going to be denied."

Brown posted a 28-21 victory here last season to snap a six-game losing streak in the series and looked poised to do it again in front of 5,368 fans. The Bears generated three turnovers and used a 1-yard Qwentin Brown touchdown run with 13:29 left to take a 10-3 lead. Brown couldn't find a finishing touch down the stretch and followed a 14-10 defeat against Harvard here with another.

"It's a challenge, because you lose two close games in a row," Brown coach James Perry said. "They're mature kids. We'll be ready to go next week."

The Bears seemed to have all the momentum after Tommy Dunn's power rush off the defense's left edge forced URI quarterback Tyler Budge's second fumble of the afternoon. Dunn recovered himself at the Rams 13 and Childs picked up a fourth down before Brown slammed into the end zone. The Rams stopped their quarterback rotation at that point and went exclusively to former Barrington standout Alex McClelland, who authored each of the last two scoring drives.

"I told the guys pregame both my parents went to Brown, and it just kind of rubbed me the wrong way that they didn't want me," McClelland said. "More than happy to be with these guys right here and this coach."

URI's second play on the ensuing series saw McClelland look for a fellow All-State pick from seasons past. He found Marquis Buchanan running free down the middle, and the Classical alum – who came in nursing a right knee injury and left briefly in the first quarter – sped 68 yards to the Bears 12. McClelland took it himself the rest of the way at the game was knotted again with 12:05 left.

"[Buchanan is] so tough," Fleming said. "People don't know that. He's one of those pretty guys who catches a lot of touchdowns – no. That's a tough dude."

Brown had a chance to reclaim the lead on the ensuing drive. The Bears rattled off nine plays before facing a fourth and five at the Rams 23 and declined to give Drew Crabtree a chance at a 40-yard field goal. James Murphy rolled right and found Levi Linowes for nine yards, but two penalties on the play – the second for a chop block in the backfield – pushed Brown out of range and forced a punt.

"All those decisions are very tight," Perry said. "We have a very good kicker – that's a long one. At this level, anything over 40 is long."

Groff's first make with 18 seconds left in the first half gave URI (3-3) a 3-0 lead into halftime. The Rams staggered on offense with Buchanan, Terrence Campbell (right ankle) and Aboraa Kwarteng (left leg) all on the sidelines but leaned on their defense to remain in contact. The Bears finished the day with just 35 rushing yards on 26 carries and threw an interception to Ethan McCann-Carter in the third quarter.

"We've had this one circled for a long time," URI defensive lineman Case Mankins said. "We had to go get it for coach."

Brown (1-2) used a big hit on the perimeter from Brock Owen to force Budge's first fumble inside its own 10, and the Bears followed with their best drive to that point. EJ Perez's recovery set up a Murphy scramble out of jail for 13 yards and a pass down the middle to Childs for 27 yards. Crabtree's 33-yard field goal with 3:11 left in the third made it a 3-3 game, and Brown seemed a couple of possessions away from shaking a URI team looking to avoid three straight defeats for the first time since 2021.

"We played a very tight football game with a quality opponent, a rival, and found a way to beat them," Fleming said. "We've got the cup sitting in Kingston where it will stay."

RI – Alex McClelland 12 run (Groff kick)

Passing: B, 21-37-1 271 (James Murphy 21-37-1 271); RI, 16-26-1 157 (Alex McClelland 6-11-0 83, Tyler Budge 10-15-1 74).

Rushing: B, 26-35 (Matt Childs 13-37, Qwentin Brown 3-3); RI, 50-217 (Gabe Winowich 23-85, BJ Barrow 8-42).

Receiving: B, 21-271 (Childs 6-64, Pearson Hill 4-33, Jadon Garza-Pender 3-66); RI, 16-157 (Marquis Buchanan 5-90, Kevin Green Jr. 3-20, Sean Byrd 2-36).
